tossups.text: This theory is defended with the concept of "primitive notions" in a series of letters that began with a request to explain how this position accounts for "voluntary actions." This theory is compared to beliefs about the "English Constitution" and the "Average Taxpayer" in a book that calls it the "official doctrine." The objection that conceivability does not entail metaphysical possibility is often raised against an argument for the "property" type of this position; that argument by David Chalmers uses the concept of "p-zombies." Princess Elizabeth of Bohemia was the first to raise the "interaction problem" for this position. This theory rests on a "category mistake" according to Gilbert Ryle, who dubbed it "the ghost in the machine." For 10 points, the pineal gland is key to what theory of René Descartes that mind and body are separate substances?
acceptableAnswers: more specific answers like Cartesian dualism

tossups.text: After this leader's brother-in-law was upset at this leader's open affair, he died in a helicopter crash that was caused by explosives planted by this leader's forces. Early in his life, this leader escaped to Syria after participating in an unsuccessful assassination attempt on his country's prime minister. The army of this leader's country invaded its eastern neighbor after a dispute over the Shatt al-Arab waterway in a war in which chemical weapons were used against the Kurds. Later, this leader's army invaded Kuwait which prompted a U.S. invasion under George H.W. Bush's administration. For 10 points, name this former Ba'athist dictatorial leader of Iraq.

One painting by this man depicts a sofa on a wood floor that stands in for Mae West's lips. In another painting by this man, a fish jumps out of water to eat a tiger. In addition to creating Dream Caused by the Flight of a Bee Around a Pomegranate a Second Before Awakening, this man depicted 28 copies of the Venus De Milo in The Hallucinogenic Toreador. Against a backdrop of the cliffs of Catalonia, this artist depicted ants swarming a pocket watch and several melting clocks. For 10 points, name this Spanish surrealist of The Persistence of Memory.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for nasal cavity and sinuses. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this pharynx-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The pharynx is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in nasal cavity and sinuses.

tossups.text: This document notes that "indirect taxes weigh heavily upon the people" and calls for a single progressive income tax. It notes that one group is "confining its activity within national bounds" but recognizes the "international character" of its aims. Perhaps the most controversial section of this document asserts that it pursues its goals "by every lawful means." One person found this document overly influenced by Ferdinand Lassalle and recommended that the Eisenachers reject it, in a letter that outlined the "dictatorship of the proletariat" and coined the phrase "from each according to his ability, to each according to his need." For 10 points, name this 1875 political manifesto, which was replaced in 1891 by the Erfurt program and was "critiqued" by Karl Marx.
acceptableAnswers: the 1875 platform of the German Social Democratic Party

tossups.text: In a story by this author, two afterlife officials mistakenly kill the protagonist with a stroke meant for Henry Barrett and send him back to life with the title body parts. This author wrote about a long object that is boiled and stomped on before having millet-like beads of fat extracted. A thief created by this author of "Horse Legs" claims to have lured a victim by promising cheap goods like mirrors buried under a mountain. In a story by this non-Russian author of "The Nose," a man steals clothes from an old crone after watching her rip hairs from a corpse for a wig. Witnesses including a traveling priest and a woodcutter testify to a police commissioner in a story by this author comprised of seven conflicting accounts of a samurai's death. For 10 points, name this Japanese author of "In A Grove" and "Rashomon."

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for oxygen diffusion. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diffusion-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diffusion is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in oxygen diffusion.

tossups.text: This organelle can be experimentally removed by using Brefeldin A to block the activation of ARFs. One model of this organelle sees it as many sections defined by RAB GTPases. Anterograde transport to this organelle is facilitated by vesicles coated by COPII ("COP-two"). This structure adds mannose-6-phosphate to proteins destined for the lysosome. Most O-linked glycosylation happens in this organelle, which is made up of stacks of cisternae and whose cis face receives input from the endoplasmic reticulum. For 10 points, name this organelle that packages proteins into membrane-bound organelles and is named after its Italian discoverer.

this structure is essential for smooth muscle locations. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this sarcomere-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The sarcomere is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in smooth muscle locations.

tossups.text: At the beginning of this dialogue, the speaker asks listeners to not be surprised if they talk like they do in the marketplace, comparing it to a stranger speaking in their own dialect. In this dialogue, the speaker describes asking an avid customer of sophists if there was a teacher that could make a man's sons excel. Near the end of this dialogue, Socrates muses that he should be paid thirty minae from trustworthy guarantors. In the sole application of elenchus in this dialogue, Socrates invokes horsebreeders improving horses after Meletus claims that all other Athenians improve the young. The Phaedo and Crito are set after the events of this dialogue, in which Socrates argues against the claims that he has been promoting impiety and corrupting the youth. For 10 points, name this dialogue in which Socrates defends himself on trial.

During this religious period, tarawih are included in nightly prayers, and days begin and end with the suhur and iftar meals. This period includes Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Power, and it precedes the monthof Shawwal. During this period, believers observe the pillar of sawm, which ends with Eid al-Fitr, a day of feasting. For ten points, name this holy month in Islam during which able-bodied Muslims fast during the day.

A character in this play compares ruling a government to piloting a ship through a storm. A sentry in this play recounts seeing the title character perform a rite involving drops of wine after a dust storm had settled, leading to the title character's arrest for breaking an edict. A death in this play is announced after it is revealed that the protagonist's lover Hamon has also committed suicide. The title character's siblings include Eteocles and Ismene, and this play is set after the events of Oedipus at Colonus. Creon's anger at the burial of Polynices leads him to sentence the title character in this play. For 10 points, name this Sophocles work about a daughter of Oedipus.

René Leibowitz cited a piece by this composer that begins with the spoken line "I cannot remember everything. I must have been unconscious" as an example of music that meets the requirements of "committed art." This composer's early use of quartal harmony can be heard in an ascending theme first played by the horn in his first Chamber Symphony. This composer began using an athematic style in his Opus 11 Drei Klavierstücke("DRY kla-VEER-shtook-uh"), and he also wrote A Survivor from Warsaw. The title character is called "drunk" in the opening section of a song cycle by this composer that is accompanied by a namesake ensemble and pioneered the technique of Sprechstimme. For 10 points, name this Austrian composer of Pierrot Lunaire who developed 12-tone serialism.

After hearing a prophecy of a youth's future success, this man sneers "be we well advised to be afraid of a dream-reader?" According to one account, this man joins Rience after the youth he believes to be his son is placed on a ship by a ruler trying to kill all children born on May Day. In that story, this man's forces are lost after he is distracted by a magician and thus unable to save King Nero, and this leader is ultimately also killed when he is slain by the "Knight of the Strange Beast," King Pellinore. His third son angrily beheads his own mother after catching her in an affair with Lamorak. Some stories state that several of this man's sons are killed during the rescue of Guinevere by Lancelot, the result of which tears the Round Table apart. This man is married to Igraine's oldest daughter, Morgause, who unbeknownst to this dude, produced Mordred with King Arthur. For 10 points, name this father of Gawain, the king of Orkney and Lothian.

This designer of the angels blowing trumpets for the First Baptist Church of Boston used a pseudonym for working with Egyptian subjects, "Amilcar Hasenfratz." One of his major works is a monument to dead soldiers and was constructed from Vosgian sandstone in front of the namesake town hall. In addition to the Lion of Belfort, he designed a work in which four nereids hold up a three-level structure with globular lightbulbs skirting it. That is a work for the U.S. Botanical Gardens known as this man's fountain. He worked with Edouard Laboulaye, Eugene Viollet le Duc and Gustav Eiffel on a project celebrating the centenary of French support for the American Revolution. For 10 points, name this sculptor of Liberty Enlightening the World, which became a New York harbor monument.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for hypodermis function. It plays a key role in the integumentary system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this epidermis-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The epidermis is a key component of the Integumentary system, involved in hypodermis function.

tossups.text: A minor character in this novel is tricked into eating rabbit droppings that are put into his Sunmaid raisin box. Another character is the author of the study The Creative Spirit of the Middle Ages and shows off a copy of Hroswitha's "Dulcitus" at her house. The main character notices that her classmate "Broccoli" Detwiler has an uncircumcised penis, so she decides they can make money by showing it off to kids for a nickel a peak. She revisits her hometown of Coffee Hollow, Pennsylvania after being expelled from the University of Florida, and reminisces on Carolyn Simpson, the head cheerleader at Lauderdale High, as well as her redneck friend Leroy Denman. In the end, the documentary film created by Molly Bolt is ignored and most of her lesbian lovers deny their feelings for her. This novel is titled for the slang term she uses for her genitals, because she thinks they're simply delicious. For 10 points, name this 1973 picaresque masterpiece by Rita Mae Brown.

The Dominican dish los tres golpes is made by boiling this food, then topping it with red onions. This food is used to create a ketchup in the Philippines which is dyed red to look like regular ketchup. This food is fried to make pisang goreng in Indonesia. Along with vanilla ice cream, this food is used in an American dessert named for Richard Foster. The leaves of this food's plant are used in the pepes cooking method. This food's Gros Michel ("grow mee-SHELL") variety was wiped out in the 1950s by an outbreak of Panama Disease, which is also threatening this food's Cavendish variety. This food used to make tostones is produced by companies such as Dole and Chiquita. For 10 points, name this curved yellow fruit.

One disease caused by damage to this structure manifests with macroorchidism, protruding ears and elongated faces. One disorder said to be linked to this structure is diagnosed with an Ishihara test, whilst webbed necks and "shield chest" are characteristic of a syndrome in which a full complement of these is not present. This structure may be Lyonised to form an inactive Barr body. Unlike Turner syndrome, Klinefelter's syndrome is caused when males possess too many of this object. For 10 points, what chromosome do females usually possess two of, and males only one?

A story by this author ends with the servant Kasparson sharing a kiss with the noble Miss Malin before a "strip of blue between the boards" signals the flooding of the title North Sea island. Martine is horrified after finding a turtle purchased by the title character of another story by this author. The character Kamante converts to Christianity and becomes a chef after being treated at a Protestant hospital in a novel by this author, who also wrote about the title French refugee spending ten thousand francs on cooking a lavish meal. This author included the story "The Deluge at Norderney" in her Seven Gothic Tales. For 10 points, name this Danish author of "Babette's Feast" who wrote about running a coffee plantation in Kenya in the memoir Out of Africa

parts.text: Name this prophet who spent three days and three nights in the belly of a large fish.
Jonah preached to the inhabitants of this city. After its inhabitants finally listened to him, they put on sackcloth, fasted, and prayed, leading god to spare the city.

This text says the whale died when he swallowed Jonah and was resurrected when it spat him out. This text was published by Moses de Leon, who said it was compiled by Simon bar Yohai while hiding in a cave.

bonuses.leadin: In one incident, the sea calms after this man is thrown overboard, and before he dies God briefly orders a plant to give him shade from the sun. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this term that, in an interview with Anna Louise Strong, was repopularized by Mao Zedong to describe the threat of the United States atomic bomb as "very powerful" in appearance, yet "unable to withstand the wind and the rain."

Mao criticized this man's appeasement of the United States, to which this man reportedly replied "the paper tiger has nuclear teeth." This man also denounced the "cult of personality" of his predecessor in a speech which allegedly gave some people heart attacks.
The Sino-Soviet split initially began after Khrushchev and Mao diverged in their interpretations of this leader's theory of communism. This man was the first premier of the Soviet Union.

bonuses.leadin: The first English translation of this phrase was recorded by Robert Morrison in his Vocabulary of the Canton Dialect. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this painting that depicts Édouard Dujardin and La Macarona seated around a table. The artist of this painting also created a poster for the cabaret where this painting is set.
This diminutive French artist of La Goulue and Waiting at Grenelle painted At the Moulin-Rouge.
Toulouse-Lautrec's La Goulue is usually identified with this artistic style. This turn of the century "total art style" was used by Hector Guimard for entrances to the Paris Metro.

bonuses.leadin: A woman with an astonishingly green face peers at the viewer from this work's right foreground. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with coronary arteries.
What is the main function of the atrium in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to coronary arteries.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Identify this author who examined the history of Western European attitudes toward table manners, bodily functions, and other matters of etiquette in his two-volume magnum opus The Civilizing Process.

In The Civilizing Process, Elias used this term to refer to the various behaviors and dispositions that societal structures condition into individuals. Pierre Bourdieu elaborated upon this concept in works like Distinction.
Bourdieu was inspired by this French thinker, who defined habitus as the aspects of culture that are anchored in the body. He's more famous, however, for his anthropological essay The Gift.

bonuses.leadin: No less an authority than Wikipedia claims that this thinker, who collaborated with Eric Dunning on The Quest for Enlightenment, wrote the founding work of figurational sociology. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author of The Kitchen God's Wife and The Bonesetter's Daughter who also created the PBS series Sagwa, the Chinese Siamese Cat.
This novel by Amy Tan details the immigrant experiences of four mother-daughter pairs as they play mahjong in San Francisco.
This character in The Joy Luck Club, a chess prodigy and rival of Jing-mei Woo in her childhood, worries about her mother Lindo's acceptance of her fiancé Rich.

bonuses.leadin: In her essay "Fish Cheeks," this author writes about her insecurities during a Christmas Eve dinner hosted by her Chinese American family and attended by a white American family. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with smooth muscle locations.
What is the main function of the sarcomere in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to smooth muscle locations.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Name this part of the cell that surrounds the cytoplasm. This structure is comprised of a phospholipid bilayer.

The plasma membrane contains many of these microdomains that play essential roles in signal transduction. These features contain more glyco-sphingo-lipids and are more tightly packed than the rest of the membrane.

Lipid rafts also contain three to five times as much of this steroid than the surrounding bilayer. More generally, this molecule helps maintain the fluidity of plasma membranes in response to changes in temperature.

bonuses.leadin: The distribution of proteins in this structure is described by the fluid mosaic model. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with autoimmune diseases.
What is the main function of the vaccine in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to autoimmune diseases.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name these "perceived" entities from metaphysics that can be described by bundle theory or substance theory. According to Descartes, these entities are observed by a subject.

The metaphysician Graham Harman rejected the privileging of human existence over that of non-human objects in founding an "object-oriented" version of this philosophical subfield, which focuses on being. One goal of this subfield is determining what exists.

Earlier thinkers like Franz Brentano and Tadeusz ("tah-DAY-oosh") Kotarbiński elucidated this ontological position that only things exist. This position denies the existence of entia rationis, or objects only existing in thought.

bonuses.leadin: Timothy Morton gave examples such as global warming and styrofoam in describing a "hyper-" type of these entities that are so widely distributed in time and space that they transcend specificity. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this work, named for a Biblical beast.
Leviathan was written by this English philosopher.
Social contract theory was foreshadowed in the Platonic dialogue Crito, in which this Athenian refuses to escape his death sentence because he must abide by the laws of his state.

bonuses.leadin: This work promoted a social contract between a government and its people, noting that the resulting strong central government could prevent a war of "all against all." For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this play featuring Shelly Levene and Ricky Roma. The eventual plot of this work focuses on a robbery at the office where Levene and Roma work.
Glengarry Glen Ross is a play by this author, known for his realistic and vulgar dialogue. Another of his plays, American Buffalo, centers on the theft of a coin collection.
Like Disgrace, this Mamet play deals with a professor accused of sexual harassment. In this play, the smug professor John is accused by his confused student Carol.

bonuses.leadin: One character in this play is the insecure James Lingk. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this composer whose most popular setting of the Gloria is the one in D major numbered 589 in the Ryom-Verzeichnis, or RV, catalogue used to record his music.
Vivaldi's collection The Contest Between Harmony and Invention includes this set of four violin concertos about the divisions of the year.
Vivaldi's L'estro armonico is a set of this many concertos for one, two, or four solo violins. Incidentally, this is also the number of notes in the chromatic scale.

bonuses.leadin: 9. This composer's Opus 10 is a collection of six flute concertos such as "Il gardellino," "La notte," and "La tempesta di mare." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these brothers, Hunahpu (wah-nuh-pwuh) and Xbalanque (sheh-bay-lan-kay), who defeated the lords of the underworld Xibalba (she-ball-bah) in a ball-game.
The Hero Twins shot out this god's jeweled set of false teeth with a blowgun and replaced them with corn, causing him to die of shame. They also defeated his sons Zipacna and Cabrakan.

In Mayan art, this article of clothing is used to identify the Hero Twins and their close relatives. In The Maya Scribe and His World, Michael Coe nicknamed the Hero Twins after this item of clothing.
acceptableAnswers: items that might look similar like “bandanas”

bonuses.leadin: These people got revenge for their older half-brothers placing them on an anthill by turning them into monkeys. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this broad style of 20th century Islamic art which combines traditional calligraphy with modernist abstraction. Its name comes from a word meaning "letter."
Artists from this country's Saqqakhaneh ("sak-kah-HAH-neh") movement explored similar themes to Hurufiyya. Many of its cities, such as Tabriz, are world-famous centers of carpet making.
acceptableAnswers: as it was still known at the time

parts.text: Many Hurufiyya works use this Arabic calligraphy style, whose highly angular form makes it ideal for abstraction or forming into squares. This style is named for the Iraqi city where it was invented.

bonuses.leadin: Though originally used to refer to so-called "Abstract Vandalism," the term "calligraffiti" has been widely applied to street art adaptations of this style in the Arabic world. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with platelets and clotting.
What is the main function of the erythrocyte in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to platelets and clotting.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: The Oulipo novel A Void was written without using this vowel, which is the most frequently used letter in both French and English.
A Void is by this French author who also wrote Life: A User's Manual.
Jean Lescure ("less-KOOR") invented an Oulipo technique in which every noun in a text is replaced with the nth noun following it in a dictionary, where n is this number.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the French literary movement Oulipo ("oo-lee-poh"), for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this second most populous city of Germany. It makes up its own German state, with Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony as its two neighbors.
acceptableAnswers: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg

parts.text: A planned concert hall in the HafenCity is named for this river, on whose waterfront it will lie. This river flows from the Krkonose ["ker-KO-no-shay"] mountains into the North Sea.

The Krkonose mountains are at Poland's border with this country, which owns a part of Hamburg docklands thanks to the Treaty of Versailles. This modern-day country's historical regions include Moravia and Bohemia.

bonuses.leadin: An urban renewal project in this city aims to convert a port district into the HafenCity, which includes its historic "warehouse city" or Speicherstadt. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The addition of an acyl chloride to an aromatic ring, like benzene, is the acylation type of this reaction, while another type involves the alkylation of the ring.

Friedel-Crafts reactions take place when acyl chlorides are reacted with this type of acid catalyst. This definition of acids and bases is based on whether the substance in question can accept or donate a pair of electrons.

Although the bonds in benzene alternate between single and double bonds, all of its bonds have been seen to be roughly 140 picometers due to the superposition of its two Lewis structures, which are collectively called this.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following questions concerning our favorite aromatic hydrocarbon--benzene, For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poem that begins "Strange now to think of you, gone without corsets & eyes," written for the death of the poet's mother, Naomi.

This other poem by the author of "Kaddish" describes a creature "whose breast is a cannibal dynamo," named Moloch, and opens with the line "I saw the best minds of my generation destroyed by madness."
"Kaddish" and "Howl" are by this poet of the Beat movement.

bonuses.leadin: The speaker of this poem realizes that "Death is the remedy all singers dream of" while listening to Ray Charles and reading "Adonais." For 10 points each:
